Explain the term "Genetic code is degenerate". (3 marks)
The genetic code is degenerate because multiple codons can encode a single amino acid (e.g., leucine and serine are each encoded by six different codons).
Genetic Code: The codon-amino acid correspondence is referred to as the genetic code.

qs.q: How do direct DNA-interacting mutagens like Methyl nitrosoguanidine (NTG) primarily alter genetic code processing?
o: By forming covalent bonds between adjacent thymine bases
By breaking the phosphodiester backbone on both strands
By physically pushing adjacent bases apart to cause deletions
By adding methyl groups to guanine, changing its pairing properties
qs.e: Methyl nitrosoguanidine (NTG) adds methyl groups to guanine, making it pair with thymine instead of cytosine. Intercalating agents are responsible for physically pushing bases apart and causing frameshifts.

qs.q: Who discovered the wobble hypothesis in 1966, explaining how the genetic code possesses flexibility at the third nucleotide position?
qs.e: Francis Crick discovered the wobble hypothesis in 1966, which explains how one amino acid can be coded by multiple codons via the third nucleotide position. Watson and Franklin are famous for discovering the DNA double helix structure.
